Anatomic Site: Left temporal lobe
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 10-year-old girl with a brain tumor - astrocytoma, undergoing temporal craniotomy and partial removal
of the tumor.

The specimen is received fresh in one part, labeled with the patient's name,
medical record number, and 'left temporal mass,' and

Anatomic Site:Parietal lobe biopsy (FS)
Parietal Tumor (FS   perm)
Clinical Diagnosis/History:
The patient is a 58-year-old male with a right parietal lesion. Per review
of the electronic medical record (MedTrack and
PathNet), the patient has experienced intermittent headaches and visual disturbances. MRI scans
revealed a 1.5 cm irregularly enhancing
lesion in the right parietal lobe which was monitored with periodic imaging.
Following notable enlargement over a 4 month period, he
underwent a stereotactic biopsy revealing an astrocytoma most consistent with
anaplastic astrocytoma, WHO Grade III (P12-3456). He
now proceeds with surgical resection.
Gross Description:
The specimen is received fresh in two parts, labeled with the patient's name
and medical record number.
Part A is additionally labeled 'parietal biopsy FS #1,' and consists of three
fragments of unoriented, irregular, gray-white and
pink-red soft tissue (0.6 x 0.6 x 0.3 cm in aggregate). A portion of the
tissue is submitted for frozen section FS1(A) with the
frozen section remnant submitted in cassette A1. The remaining unfrozen
tissue is entirely submitted in cassette A2.
Part B is additionally labeled 'parietal tumor (FS and perm)' and comprises
multiple fragments of unoriented, irregular,
white-pink and gray-red tissue (2.0 x 1.5 x 0.4 cm in aggregate). A portion
of the tissue is submitted for frozen section
FS2(B) with the frozen section remnant submitted in cassette B1. The
remaining unfrozen tissue is entirely submitted in
cassette B2. (abc)
The immunoperoxidase stain(s) reported above were developed and their
performance characteristics determined by the Stanford Medical
Center Department of Pathology. They have not been cleared or approved by the
U. S. Food and Drug Administration. The FDA has
determined that such clearance or approval is not necessary. These tests are
used for clinical purposes. They should not be
regarded as investigational or for research. This laboratory is certified
under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments
of 1988 ('CLIA') as qualified to perform high-complexity clinical testing.
Diagnosis Comments:
Best demonstrated on section B2 is an astrocytic neoplasm characterized by
alternating microcystic regions and compact areas
with spindle-shaped tumor cells with fine fibrillary processes. Occasional Rosenthal
fibers are observed. There are vessels with notable
endothelial prominence, a feature associated with anaplastic astrocytoma.
 While some pleomorphic nuclei are present,
they are not predominant, and mitotic activity is limited.
Immunohistochemical stains are conducted and assessed on block B2. A
neurofilament stain is largely negative for
background axons but at the margins, neuropil is well defined. GFAP
is positive in a subset of tumor cells with
elongated processes, p53 reveals sparse positive nuclei and a MIB-1
labeling index is estimated at approximately 3%, supporting
an anaplastic astrocytoma diagnosis. Additionally, a CD34 stain
highlights surrounding blood vessels and CD68 shows
peripheral clusters of microglia/macrophages.
Immunohistochemistry for IDH-1 will be performed and an addendum will follow.
Molecular studies for 1p19q status will be
conducted by the Molecular Pathology Lab, and their report will follow. Drs.
John Doe and Jane Smith have reviewed this case
and concur with the diagnosis.
Interoperative Diagnosis:
FS1  (A) Brain, parietal lobe, biopsy:  Portion of parietal cortex, negative
for neoplasm. Tissue section and cytologic
preparation. Attending Dr. Michael Johnson, 60731.
FS2  (B) Brain, parietal tumor, biopsy:  Infiltrating neoplastic astrocytes
consistent with anaplastic astrocytoma, WHO
Grade III -- no high-grade features identified. Attending Dr. Michael Johnson,
60731.
Final Diagnosis:
A.  Brain, right parietal lobe, craniotomy:  Portion of parietal cortex.
B.  Brain, right parietal lobe, craniotomy:  Astrocytoma, most consistent with
anaplastic astrocytoma, WHO Grade III; see comment.
